summary: Optimize Guardrails: customer confused by 'Timeout' gating state (does it mean quality failed?) + asks for next steps
description:
Issue summary:
Customer is piloting Optimize Guardrails gating. During an Optimize apply attempt, the UI showed gating status = "Timeout". Customer interpreted this as either (a) quality checks failed but were hidden, or (b) the optimization may have applied without checks. Customer is requesting clarification on what "Timeout" means, what to do next, and whether there is an audit trail proving checks were attempted.

Customer impact:
- Blocks adoption: customer is hesitant to proceed with further Optimize applies until timeout semantics are clear.
- Trust/assurance concern: customer wants to be sure cost-saving config changes are not applied without passing evals.
- Mild operational friction: customer unsure whether to rerun, wait, or request override.

Environment:
- Tenant: northbridge-support-prod
- Region: us-east
- Console: Optimize > Apply recommendation
- Optimization type: caching + batching tweak (as proposed by Optimize)
- Target route: /v1/chat/completions (workload tagged: support-chat)

What customer saw:
- Gate status: Timeout
- UI message (customer quote): "Evaluation timed out. Try again later."
- No visible detail on whether any metrics ran or if partial results exist.

Steps to reproduce (per customer):
1) Open Redwood Console > Optimize recommendations
2) Select recommendation "Enable prefix cache + increase max_batch_tokens"
3) Click "Run checks and apply"
4) Wait ~8–10 minutes, then UI flips to "Timeout" and apply is blocked

Support questions to answer:
1) Does "Timeout" mean quality failed? (No)
2) Was the config change applied anyway? (No; apply is blocked)
3) Are there audit logs showing the eval run was triggered and what timed out? (Yes; internal today, customer-facing export pending)
4) What should customer do next? (Rerun; if urgent, request override with justification per pilot policy)

Initial investigation notes:
- We see elevated eval-runner queue latency in us-east around the time of the attempt.
- The apply flow appears to have correctly blocked (no config diff committed).
- Console copy is ambiguous and does not state clearly that "Timeout" is an infrastructure/system failure state (not a quality regression) and that no changes were applied.

Ask / escalation:
- Platform team to confirm official semantics for Timeout and align UI + API messaging.
- Evaluate whether timeout thresholds are too aggressive for some suites and whether the system should return partial results / clearer instructions.

Attachments/links:
- Slack: #support thread referencing pilot gating timeouts (internal)
- Internal run id: gr_run_01HNRX5Z8Q9S4P4E0K9K (support-only reference)
- Candidate docs update: clarify gating states (Pass/Fail/Timeout) and recommended action.
comments: 2025-01-16 09:12 (Owen Phillips, Support): Customer reached out via email after seeing "Timeout" in Optimize Guardrails. They believe it might mean "quality failed" or that the system applied without checks. I confirmed we are investigating and asked for timestamp/route/model details. Set expectation: response within 1 business day.

2025-01-16 10:03 (Owen Phillips, Support): Added customer details from console screenshots: us-east, model redwood-llama-3-70b-instruct, recommendation was caching+batching. They waited ~8–10 minutes. UI provided no guidance besides "try again later".

2025-01-16 11:26 (Brian Murphy, Platform - API gating plumbing): Checked control-plane audit stream for tenant northbridge-support-prod at timestamp. I do NOT see a config commit event for that apply attempt. I do see OptimizeConfigChangeRequested followed by GuardrailsEvaluationStarted then GuardrailsEvaluationTimedOut (worker deadline exceeded). So apply blocked as intended; the issue is UX semantics + reliability of eval runner backlog.

2025-01-16 11:44 (Sean Gallagher, SRE): Confirming we had transient queue buildup in eval-runner us-east due to a noisy retry loop from one suite selector bug. Mitigated by draining + temporarily lowering concurrency. This was not a customer traffic incident (guardrails-only). Suggest we message customer: timeout means system couldn’t complete checks; no changes were applied; rerun should succeed now.

2025-01-16 12:10 (Ethan Park, Control Plane): +1 on semantics. Timeout should be treated as "inconclusive" and default behavior for enterprise pilot is "blocked" (unless override allowed). We should update console copy to explicitly say: "No changes were applied" and provide a "Rerun checks" CTA + optional "Request override" (role-gated).

2025-01-16 13:05 (Owen Phillips, Support -> Customer draft): Proposed wording to send: Timeout != Fail; no config change applied; we attempted to run eval checks but infrastructure didn’t return within our deadline; rerun now; if urgent, we can process an override with justification and full audit logging. Waiting for Platform to confirm official copy.

2025-01-17 09:22 (Kenji Nakamura, UX): The current string is too similar to quality failure. We should separate states: "System timeout" vs "Quality regression". Suggest copy: "Checks couldn’t complete in time. We did not apply the optimization." Also add link to "View run details" (even if empty/partial).

2025-01-17 10:14 (Brian Murphy, Platform): Filed internal follow-up to adjust API error payload for TIMEOUT to include explicit `applied=false` and `next_actions=[rerun, request_override]`. This should reduce confusion for API users too. Related work tracks to console states in pr_18502 and safe-degrade logic pr_18571.

2025-01-17 14:37 (Owen Phillips, Support): Sent response to customer explaining semantics and confirming no change was applied. Offered to rerun checks together and to provide an audit export screenshot for this specific attempt if needed.

2025-01-20 08:55 (Owen Phillips, Support): Customer acknowledged and retried; rerun passed within ~3 minutes and apply completed successfully. They asked that we update messaging in the UI before expanding pilot to additional teams. Marking ticket resolved; keeping feedback loop open.
resolution:
Resolved with customer after clarifying semantics: "Timeout" is an infrastructure/eval-runner completion failure (inconclusive), not a quality failure. In Timeout state, Optimize apply is blocked and no config changes are committed. Customer retried after queue stabilization and gating passed.

Follow-ups:
- Platform/Console to update UI + API messaging to explicitly state "No changes applied" and provide clearer next actions (rerun/request override) (tracked via related PRs).
- SRE to continue tuning eval-runner queue/timeout thresholds during pilot and alert on backlog to prevent recurrence.
